title: Proper cohomology restriction to the closed-point scheme of a weakly contractible test base
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, with the discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring uses all continuous maps from profinite sets. For a scheme $T$ put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$, using ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and the small-site/indexing universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal P_T$ be the intersection of all replete classes in $\mathcal A_T$ containing zero and all finite constant scalar-model constructible modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible], closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between members, extensions, and all small ambient coproducts. Extension closure means that in $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ membership of both ends implies membership of the middle. 
Let $Y$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], and $w:W=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$ an affine w-contractible object of $Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ [sk-def-pe-wlocal, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Put $J=\bigcap_{\mathfrak m\text{ maximal}}\mathfrak m$ and $C=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$, with its quotient closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow W$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $C$ is affine, reduced, zero-dimensional and w-contractible, its residue fields are separably closed, and $|C|$ is exactly the closed-point subspace of $|W|$. Put $X_W=X\times_YW$ and $X_C=X\times_YC$, with projection $a:X_C\to X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $M\in\mathcal P_X$, the canonical restriction morphism is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$:
$$R\Gamma(X_W,M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma((X_C)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},a^*M).$$
On the left, $X_W\to X$ is an object of $X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ and $R\Gamma(X_W,-)$ means the right derived evaluation functor $N\mapsto N(X_W)$ in $\mathcal A_X$. On the right it means right derived global sections in $\mathcal A_{X_C}$. The map is the derived restriction map induced by the exact module inverse image along $a$, with the pulled-back coefficient identification; it agrees in degree zero with restricting a section from $X_W$ to $X_C$. No completeness of $M$, finite presentation of $f$, invertibility of $\ell$, Noetherianity, or field of definition is assumed. Empty schemes are allowed.

proof.text: For a w-local ring J equals the vanishing ideal of the closed points. Since the closed points are closed, V(J) is exactly that set. The quotient is reduced, its spectrum is affine, and all its primes are maximal. Apply Jacobson henselianity and henselian invariance of w-contractibility. Strict henselianity of the quotient at its maximal ideals gives separably closed residue fields. The surjective quotient map is a closed immersion, whose range is V(J).

Write $T=X_W$, $T_0=X_C$, $b:T\to X$, $t:T_0\hookrightarrow T$, $q:T\to W$, and $q_0:T_0\to C$. Base change makes $q,q_0$ proper and $t$ a closed immersion. Both bases are affine, hence qcqs. Finite type over an affine base gives a finite affine cover of each source; separatedness over that base makes all pairwise affine-open intersections affine. The affine-cover criterion therefore makes $T,T_0$ qcqs. This verifies the geometric hypotheses of the relative coefficient-transfer lemma; it does not require $Y$ itself to be quasi-separated.

proof.text: Pullback pasting makes the specified properClosedFibreMap the base change of the quotient immersion. Apply lem-sfb-proper-wcontractible-torsion-rigidity to its proper structural map. This supplies the actual torsion cohomologyMap bijections.

FiniteConstantStratifiedZariskiLocality provides pullback of finite stratifications and gluing from affine neighborhoods. Around t in T choose an affine neighborhood V of b(t) and an affine neighborhood W contained in its inverse image. The inverse-image composition isomorphism identifies restriction to W of b-star M with pullback from V. This gives constructibility of b-star M. Exactness and preservation of coproducts make the inverse image of the weak Serre coproduct closure a qualifying class; minimality gives preservation of the closure.

Apply the closed torsion-rigidity coefficient-transfer lemma to $(T,T_0,t)$, using step 2 for qcqs and closedness, step 3 for every torsion étale sheaf and step 4 for $b^*M\in\mathcal P_T$. It gives the canonical derived restriction isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},b^*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma((T_0)_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},t^*b^*M).$$
The coefficient topology here is exactly the topology in the item. This step uses the stated coefficient-transfer obligation, not a replacement by complete or solid coefficients.

proof.text: Apply lem-sfb-weakly-etale-derived-evaluation-restriction to b:T -> X, the specified t and a. Exact b-star commutes with the degree-zero single functor. Naturality transports invertibility of the coefficient-transfer component at (b-star M)[0] to b-star(M[0]). The localization equivalence then gives precisely the original properClosedFibreDerivedRestriction at M[0].

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NA-f2dc6ca38 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read in full: the item, both new nodes, the statements of all 29 proof_deps, the blueprint place (refinement proof (2)), and RTW §1.1, Prop. 1.1.2 and Cor. 1.1.5. Steps 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8 are correct as written. Step 1: V(J) equals the closure of W^c, which is W^c because W^c is closed; C has the same extremally disconnected π0 as W, and its local rings are separably closed fields. Step 2: base change, affine-cover and separatedness arguments give qcqs without assuming Y quasi-separated. Step 4: projectivity of the representables plus the abelian étale/pro-étale comparison give exact étale global sections on W and C. Step 5: torsion proper base change (thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below), then Leray with exact Γ, then henselian H^0. Step 8: slice localization plus K-injective restriction. Repairs, both small and in the item's proof only: step 3 now states that the identity of W is a closed immersion, hence proper by lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence (c), and that its closed fibre is C (uses updated). Step 6 (E1, small): T is qcqs, so the constructibility definition needs one global finite stratification; the step now glues the pulled-back affine-local strata over a finite affine cover as (V_k \ ∪_{j<k} V_j) ∩ S, which are constructible because quasi-compact opens of a qcqs scheme are retrocompact. New node lem-sfb-wcontractible-jacobson-henselian is true (RTW 1.1.2: W is its own henselization along W^c), uses the idempotent definition, and is not a duplicate of lem-zl-henselian-wstrict-local-invariance or lem-zl-condensed-henselian-lisse-rigidity. New node lem-sfb-closed-torsion-rigidity-serre-transfer is a generic transfer for any qcqs closed pair, not a clause of the item; it follows the landed lem-sfb-torsion-cd-topological-serre-transfer pattern. Tested t = id, T0 empty (forces T empty), Λ finite (P stays classical), Z_ℓ by Rlim, rationals by lattices; no counterexample found. Closure under kernels and the norm-topology Ω are not routine, but both are inherited from the item's statement, which already marked its source WANTED. Batch-5 flag: thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below is torsion proper base change, given by neither assumption; it reaches sec-poincare-duality only via lem-pod-lisse-module-sheaves-as-module-objects, a generic statement that lisse sheaves are module objects of FLC(Y) and not a step of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so the flag is accepted. The 27 generic tool_uses are accepted. Maintainer note: the WANTED coefficient-transfer obligations (cd and rigidity) carry the real difficulty of the qcqs heart-bound chain.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
